reference_items.justification: Capped at 2 by SCORING.md 1.1 (a triggered hard fail caps the item at 2); the item's own min-over-axes aggregation gives 0. The formula and the civilian half are real and were measured live, which is why this is not scored 0: the civilian suspicion fill responds correctly to light (V 0.5335 vs 0.0500 -> CHALLENGE at 0.83 s vs 8.67 s, a 10.4x response to a 10.7x V), to contextWeight (3.00 vs 1.60 -> ALARM 6.67 s vs 12.42 s, 1.86x against a predicted 1.875x), to distance (15 m never reaches CHALLENGE in 20 s), to the sight cone (civilian facing away: suspicion 0.00 after 20 s) and to raceSuspicion (naga/saxhleel 1.49x against 1.481 predicted; saxhleel/imperial 1.69x against 1.687). What fails is everything the item's own method names: method 2 asks for an INFANTRY at 8 m and the frame of first AGGRO, and the INFANTRY reaches AGGRO at frame 30 (0.50 s) identically at V=0.6669 and V=0.0500 (item: 1.03 s and 26.7 s) because the enemy alert meter fills at a flat +4/frame inside its sight radius and never reads V; method 4's no-proximity-leak assertion fails live (AGGRO at 1.0 m behind, in the dark, crouched, at Sneak 100); method 3 is unrunnable because `alert_channel` is absent from the enemy record and because nothing hears continuous movement at all (a civilian 2 m away, facing away, after 10 s of sprinting in heavy armour on dry reed at r_effective 36.31 m: suspicion 0.00); method 6's four search behaviours do not exist in the world (the enemy's alert decays 100 -> 0 in 2 s, its speed is 0.00 m/s and its position never leaves the spawn anchor over 24 s, and zone_baseline_alert stays 0); method 9's whole bypass census is unmeasurable and 0.
reference_items.why_not_ten: The visibility term is computed once per frame into the trace and no entity in the running game multiplies anything by it. Measured coupling between V and enemy detection is exactly 0.00 (critic-w1-15.json, RI-STL01-M2-enemy-detection). There is no NPC search behaviour of any kind, no hearing channel for continuous movement, and no line-of-sight occlusion term anywhere in the model (`in_cover` is an authored boolean worth x0.80).
reference_items.path_to_ten: 1) In game/src/sim/entities.js's perception branch replace `e.alert += 4` with `baseFill(sim.stealth.p.V, d, R)/60` from sim/stealth/detection.js and re-run RI-STL01 method 2 AS WRITTEN (one INFANTRY at 8 m, five configurations) to land within 5% of {1.03, 3.94, 8.5, 26.7, 26.7} s, and method 4 to end at alert == 0. 2) Route the continuous sound radius into the same fill and add `alert_channel` to the enemy record so method 3's binary search is runnable. 3) Invoke sim/stealth/search.js from the step when an alerted entity loses contact, so S-1..S-4 are observable in a trace rather than only in a module. 4) Add a real occluder test between eye node and chest node so breaking line of sight works. 5) Bypass census follows encounter placement (W1-02/04/05/12).

reference_items.provenance_correction: RI-STL01 2 states V = clamp(L^0.7 * M * S * E * A, 0.05, 1.30) and then publishes five worked rows that gamma = 0.7 cannot produce. I recomputed independently: row 2 (L=0.35, M=1.45, S=0.97) gives 0.6745 at gamma 0.7 against the item's stated 0.339, and 0.3374 at gamma 1.36; row 4 (L=0.06) gives a raw 0.0733 at gamma 0.7, so the item's own '(clamped)' annotation on that row is false at the item's own exponent. The builder's AMENDMENT-W1-15-01 1 is arithmetically correct and its choice of the table over the exponent is right (three constraints against one). The item must be corrected, not the build.

reference_items.native_scale: 9 axes scored 0/6/10, aggregation min-over-axes; failure threshold: any axis below 6; lock determinism binary
reference_items.native_verdict: we lose (ownership-enforcement axis below its 6 floor)
reference_items.justification: Capped at 2 by a triggered hard fail, and it is the harshest score in this verdict to write because the lock ruling is the best-built thing in the piece. Measured live: the deterministic gate refuses below the Security requirement with 0 picks consumed and a spoken prompt; the tolerance curve reads 4.00 / 12.25 / 20.50 / 34.00 deg at Security 40/55/70/100 and clamps at exactly 34.0 at Security 140; a tier-3 collar in the loaded world opened under three timed `interact` presses over 153 f@60; and the engine's RNG counter moved by 0 across the entire interaction. The angles are authored, not generated: 719 angles over 235 locks give chi-square 226.1 on 35 df against a uniform-rejection threshold of 57.34, with 0 length mismatches and 0 duplicate vectors inside an interior; 59/59 tier-4 and tier-5 locks carry alt_routes. Seam S21's surviving die is real and it matters: 300 attempts over 60 seeds x 5 skill levels drew exactly once each, with notice_chance 0.357/0.278/0.209/0.137/0.070 at Sneak 5/25/45/70/100 and caught counts 19/17/15/8/6 of 60 — the multiplicative form does not collapse to a floor. Ownership DATA is excellent: 1,878 placed objects, 100% carrying an owner key, 100% non-null, 292 distinct owner strings, 0% single-owner interiors, 233 trespass zones in 7 classes with >= 28 per settlement. What fails is method 2, the item's own first How-we-lose: after three thefts, saveState().crime.stolen_registry is [] and saveState().inventory still contains only the starting knife. The objects are flagged at the moment of the take and then are nowhere — not in the inventory, not in the save. Fencing, which the item defines as the only thing that clears stolen_from, is therefore reachable only by handing fenceQuote() an item object the critic builds.
reference_items.why_not_ten: stolen_from is set by takeObject() and never persisted: it is absent from the save's dedicated stolen_registry field and the taken object never enters the player's inventory, so method 2's round-trip assertion cannot pass. Separately: the world ships 0 tier-1 locks against the item's ~410, and the pickpocket's geometry gates (dist, bearing, moving, target civ_state) are evaluated against arguments the caller supplies rather than against a real NPC's position.
reference_items.path_to_ten: 1) Make takeObject() move the instance into the player's inventory with owner_of_record and stolen set, and serialise the set into save.crime.stolen_registry — acceptance: take 20 owned objects, assert all 20 appear in saveState() and survive a saveState/loadState round trip (method 2 verbatim). 2) Have pickpocketBegin(targetEid) derive dist/bearing/moving/civ_state from the entity rather than accept them, and re-run method 7's sweep against a spawned civilian. 3) Author the ~410 tier-1 and ~230 tier-2 locks as interiors land. 4) Build tools/analysis/economy-model.mjs so method 10's [118,000, 136,000] thief-income band is measurable at all.

reference_items.native_scale: 12 axes scored 0/6/10, aggregation min-over-axes; failure threshold: any axis below 6; persistence, S10 handling and mid-fight accrual binary
reference_items.native_verdict: we lose (witness model and report chain below their 6 floors)
reference_items.justification: Capped at 2 by a triggered hard fail. The MODEL is the most complete thing in the piece and every number in it checks out when it is asked directly: the 17-crime schedule is exact and scales with value_g; the guard ladder reads greeting_only / arrest_dialogue / attack_on_sight at 200 / 600 / 2,000 g against an Imperial arrest threshold of 405 and an attack threshold of 1,620, with the band-3 record carrying parley: 'surrender' (seam S13); the arrest offers three answers and refuses the fourth by name ('You're 100 gold short, and I can count.'); serving 1,000 g gives 10 days, -5 levels taken one at a time from the highest cell-blocked skill, Sneak +3, Security +2, stolen goods and picks confiscated, weapons returned, and the ledger is byte-identical across two different seeds, which is the S21 assertion; S10 is priced as written (kill the only witness unobserved -> bounty 0 and the 225 g suppressed; kill them observed -> 1,000 murder + 450 doubled = 1,450); bounty survives death. What fails is the sentence the item calls its single most important structural decision. A crime does not create a bounty, a REPORT does — and no report can ever happen, because no witness is ever created by observation. Measured: a civilian 3 m from the player in daylight, at contextWeight 3.00, already at civ_state ALARM with suspicion 100, watches takeObject() succeed. Result: witnesses [], witnesses_pending 0, bounty 0 after a further 5 s, and a crime record with landed:false that nothing can ever land. Every witness in this build exists because a critic called addWitness(crimeRef, {eid, identified}). There are no guard entities, so no guard ever approaches, follows for 45 s, or attacks; getGuardBand() is a function of a number you set with setBounty().
reference_items.why_not_ten: The witness predicate in 2 — LOS, V >= 0.10, dist <= 1.4 x R, civ_state advanced this frame — is never evaluated against live entities, so methods 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are all reachable only by hand-feeding the oracle the observation it was supposed to make. Coupling between the civilian state machine (which is real) and the crime ledger (which is real) is 0.
reference_items.path_to_ten: In game/src/sim/stealth/system.js's step, on any frame where a crime-class context (handling_owned_object, lockpicking, over_fresh_corpse, or a blow on a non-hostile) produces a crime record, iterate the live civilians and guards and call crime.witness() for each whose civ_state advanced to CHALLENGE/ALARM this frame with V >= 0.10 and dist <= 1.4 x R; then drive reportRoute() from the witness entity's actual path to the nearest guard entity, and set the witness fleeing. Acceptance: RI-CRM01 method 3 passes end to end with ZERO addWitness() calls — a witness event on the crime frame, reported == false, bounty 0 until a report event, and the 120 m run landing within 10% of 35.3 s. Then method 6's identification split (V 0.45 vs 0.18 -> 1 : 0.4) and method 4's S10 pair re-run from world state.

reference_items.native_scale: 11 axes scored 0/6/10, aggregation min-over-axes; jurisdictional legality, parley, mid-fight accrual and AR-3 encounter axes binary
reference_items.native_verdict: we lose (parley coverage and the AR-3 encounter flip unmeasurable)
reference_items.justification: Capped at 2. The jurisdictional matrix — the thing the item is named for — is genuinely solved and measured: 0 of 4 sanctioning authorities is honoured in all three jurisdictions, so the Morag Tong problem does not ship; a Tong writ executed in front of an Imperial guard still yields the full 1,600 g; the exclusivity graph refuses >= 8 ordered pairs with in-fiction reasons and an exhaustive search over the 16-element join graph finds no reachable state holding three authorities (after the builder's own found defect closed one pair); Ledger interception runs 4 then refuses, with the ceiling and the reach both enforced; a ku-vastei ruling extinguishes blood-price while leaving Imperial bounty untouched; the AR-3 guard numbers land 15/15 with arrestThreshold(Naga, Xul-Aneekh 4) = 45 and arrestThreshold(Naga, Ninth Cohort 5) = 238, a 5.29x spread from faction alone. All of that is a matrix, and it is correct. What cannot be measured is everything the item makes binary and behavioural: there are no 27 sanctioned-murder targets, so the 27/27 parley assertion and the >= 18 non-lethal resolutions are unmeasurable and 0; there is no yield state to observe, so method 3's requirement that a parley event fire while player.state is a combat state is unmeasurable; and method 7's encounter test asks for a traversal scenario (wld-stone-forest-traverse) with >= 12 AGGRO transitions at rank 0 and 0 at rank 4 — the scenario does not exist and there are no war-brood camps, so the flip is verified as a disposition-threshold computation (6 + 12 regard = 18 vs 15) rather than as an observed encounter.
reference_items.why_not_ten: Four of the item's eleven axes, including three of its four binary ones, have no world to be measured in: no writ targets, no yield state, no war-brood encounters, no hunters placed. The matrix is complete and the behaviour it governs does not exist yet.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Sequence behind the pieces that own the world: (1) W1-18/W1-19 author the 27 sanctioned-murder quests with parley blocks, then re-run method 4 for 27/27 and >= 18 violence_required:false; (2) W1-12 places the war-brood camps and ships tools/harness/scenarios/wld-stone-forest-traverse.json, then re-run method 7 asserting >= 12 AGGRO at rank 0, 0 at rank 4, and identical archetype/moveset/statblock ids between the two runs; (3) W1-09's YIELD state at <= 15% HP with hitboxes going inactive, then method 3's parley event on a combat-state frame. Nothing in the matrix needs to change.

reference_items.native_scale: band 0-10 over PACIFIST-ALL / NONVIOLENT-OPTION / VERB-SPREAD / GATED / per-faction spread / verb minima / live verification; hard fails listed in Scoring
reference_items.native_verdict: hard fail (VERB-SPREAD > 40% on the tree this piece shipped; live verification unmeasurable)
reference_items.justification: THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THIS ITEM WAS BLOCKED ON: PACIFIST-ALL is no longer unmeasurable-by-dependency — RI-STL01, RI-STL02 and RI-CRM01 all exist in the build as systems the harness can drive, so the W6 amendment's blocking clause is lifted. It is still not a measurement of the game, for three separate reasons, and the number is worthless without all three stated. (1) The census population is 24 quests at this piece's own commit and 33 at HEAD, against the corpus's ~180 — and both figures read PACIFIST-ALL 100.0% and VIOLENCE-MANDATORY 0.0% purely because the only quests shipped so far are W1-14's magic-utility set and the boards, which were authored non-violent. A 100% that comes from sample selection is not a design ratio. (2) VERB-SPREAD is 42.1% at commit 140d3c6 (magic_utility holds 24 of 57 non-violent resolutions), which is the item's own promoted hard fail at > 40%; at HEAD, after W1-18 added quests this piece did not write, it falls to 28.2%. (3) The item's mandatory live verification — complete 10 pacifist quests in-engine and record the kill count — is unmeasurable in this build. The verbs this piece exists to unblock are present but far below their minima: 4 sneak resolutions and 2 steal at 140d3c6 (6 and 3 at HEAD) against a floor of 10 each and RI-STL01's SNEAK-QUESTS >= 22. biggest_gap.what: The stealth and crime models are computed beside the world instead of by it, and the coupling is measurably zero at the two places the reference items make load-bearing. (1) DETECTION: an INFANTRY at 8 m reaches alert_state AGGRO at frame 30 — 0.500 s — identically at V = 0.6669 (midday, standing, heavy armour, Sneak 5) and at V = 0.0500 (unlit, crouched, in cover, Sneak 100), with identical alert curves of 40/80/100 at f=10/20/30. RI-STL01 2's own table says those two configurations are 1.03 s and 26.7 s apart. The alert meter fills at a flat +4/frame whenever the player is inside the archetype's sight radius and cone, and never multiplies by V; the control at 30 m confirms a live entity is being driven (alert stays 0). Coupling = 0.00. The same is true of the sound model: r_effective computes to 36.31 m at the loud end and a civilian 2 m away, facing away, registers suspicion 0.00 after 10 s of sprinting in heavy armour across dry reed. (2) WITNESSES: a civilian standing 3 m from the player in full daylight, at contextWeight 3.00, already at civ_state ALARM with suspicion 100, watches takeObject() succeed on an owned object. getCrimeState() returns witnesses: [], the trace reports witnesses_pending 0, no witness event fires, and the bounty is still 0 five seconds later. The crime record exists with landed: false and can never land. Every witness that appears anywhere in this build was created by a critic calling addWitness(crime_id, {eid, identified}). The civilian suspicion machine — which IS wired, and which I measured responding correctly to light (10.4x), context weight (1.86x), distance, sight cone and raceSuspicion (1.49x and 1.69x) — and the crime ledger are two correct systems in the same process that never speak to each other.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Nothing a player does with this piece has a consequence: you cannot sneak past an enemy because the darkness it took a lighting model to compute does not reach the thing hunting you, and you can rob every house in Gideon in front of its owner and never acquire a bounty — so the 17-crime schedule, the report chain, the three arrest answers, jail and the S10 decision are all unreachable in play.

remedy.action: Two call sites, both inside code this piece owns, plus one trace field. (A) game/src/sim/entities.js, the perception branch: replace `e.alert += 4` with the shipped model — `e.alert += baseFill(sim.stealth.p.V, d, e.sight_radius_m) / 60` from game/src/sim/stealth/detection.js, with the peripheral cone scaled by 0.45 as RI-AI01 §B specifies; add the `alert_channel` field ('sight'|'peripheral'|'hearing') to the enemy trace record so a light failure can be told from a sound failure; and route the continuous sound radius (soundRadiusFor) into the same fill on the hearing channel. (B) game/src/sim/stealth/system.js, in the fixed step: whenever a crime record is created (takeObject, lockBegin, a blow on a non-hostile, standing over a corpse), iterate this.civilians and any guard entities and call this.crime.witness(crime.id, ...) for each whose civ_state advanced to CHALLENGE or ALARM this frame with V >= 0.10 and dist <= 1.4 x R(npc), setting identified from V >= 0.30; then drive reportRoute() from that entity's own path to the nearest guard entity and flip it to the fleeing behaviour.
remedy.acceptance: (A) RI-STL01 method 2 run exactly as written — one INFANTRY facing the player at 8 m, the five configurations of §2, first frame of alert_state == 'AGGRO' — lands within 5% of {1.03, 3.94, 8.5, 26.7, 26.7} s, and method 4 (crouched, unlit, still, 1.0 m behind a stationary enemy, 3,600 f@60) ends with alert == 0.000. (B) RI-CRM01 method 3 passes end to end with ZERO addWitness() calls in the script: a `witness` event on the crime frame, reported == false, bounty 0 until a `report` event fires, and the 120 m run landing within 10% of 35.3 s. Both are re-measurable with `node tools/harness/critic-w1-15.mjs`, whose RI-STL01-M2-enemy-detection and RI-CRM01-M3-witness-from-the-world blocks are written for exactly this closure; today they read coupling 0.00 and witnesses [].

secondary_observations.what: No NPC search behaviour exists in the world. After being seen and breaking contact at 60 m, the enemy's alert decays 100 -> 40 -> 0 within 2 s, its speed is 0.00 m/s and its position is unchanged at its spawn anchor for the full 24 s observed, and zone_baseline_alert stays 0. RI-STL01 7's S-1 (LKP then the plausible cover set), S-2 (8 -> 14 -> 20 m escalation), S-3 (one-hop ally raise to 45) and S-4 (the 180 s zone memory) all pass at module level in stl-probe.mjs and none of them is ever invoked by the step. An enemy that instantly forgets is one of the two named failure modes; this is that one.

reset() and loadState() do not clear this subsystem. After setBounty('imperial', 777), setCrimeContext('lockpicking') and two spawned civilians, a full reset({}) followed by loadState('default') leaves the bounty at 777, the context at 'lockpicking' and both civilians present. Every scenario that touches stealth or crime is therefore contaminated by whatever ran before it — I had to launch a fresh browser page per configuration to measure the civilian detection curve at all, and my first attempt read eight ALARM states that were one leftover civilian.

The world ships 0 tier-1 locks against RI-STL02 3c's ~410. Tiers 2/3/4/5 land at 56/120/48/11; the design-load-bearing three (120/48/11) are exact and the simplest lock in the game — the one a starting character meets first — does not exist anywhere.

The harness methods for this piece take world facts as arguments rather than deriving them: pickpocketBegin({dist, bearingDeg, moving, targetCivState}), addWitness({eid, identified}), takeObject(instance, {observedBy}), playerDeath({killedByGuardDuringArrest}), getGuardBand() over a bounty you set. Each of the resulting assertions is therefore a test of arithmetic on numbers the critic supplied. This is the mechanism by which the coupling gap stayed invisible through 191 passing builder assertions, and it is why I filed RI-MTH07.

RI-STL01 method 2 names an INFANTRY and the shipped scenario tools/harness/scenarios/stl-cone-8m.json spawns a civilian instead, whose state machine has no AGGRO state at all. The piece's status file reports 'five RI-STL01 2 rows within 0.68% of the item's own times'; those times are arithmetic on V x fill-rate, and no enemy reached AGGRO in any of them. The claim is true of the formula and false of the game.

Three builder claims survived my own instruments unchanged and should be recorded as such: (1) AMENDMENT-W1-15-01 1's light-exponent defect is arithmetically correct — I recomputed rows 2 and 4 independently and gamma = 0.7 cannot produce the item's own table, including the '(clamped)' annotation on row 4 that is false at 0.7; (2) the lock keeps no die, verified as 0 RNG draws across a complete live interaction rather than as a source read; (3) seam S21's pickpocket die is genuinely live and genuinely matters, at 0.357 -> 0.070 notice chance across Sneak 5 -> 100 with matching caught rates over 300 attempts, and the builder's note about rejecting a subtractive form that collapsed to a 2% floor is borne out by the shipped curve.

corpus_extended.note: A corpus hole, per CRITIC-DOCTRINE 7.2: no reference item requires a critic to show that a model shipped by a piece is CONSUMED by the world. Every Comparison method in the corpus is satisfied identically by a model that drives the game and by a model that sits beside it, which is how this piece passed 191 of its own assertions with a visibility term nothing reads and a witness predicate nothing calls — and, on the evidence of the W1-10 verdict in the same wave, how 87 movesets shipped unreachable. RI-MTH04 asks 'did you run it'; RI-MTH07 asks 'did the thing you ran do anything', and defines a coupling statistic, a mandatory null control, and a hand-feed audit for harness methods that accept world facts as arguments.

ORDERING: CRITIC-DOCTRINE 8 says a critic receives the builder's notes only after recording raw measurements; my task prompt handed me orchestration/status/W1-15.json and AMENDMENT-W1-15-01.md as required reading and I read both first. I treated every claim in them as a hypothesis to attack with an independent instrument — which is why the verdict contradicts the checkpoint's headline claim about method 2 and confirms its amendment arithmetic by recomputation rather than by agreement. AR-3: this piece is NOT seam-sterile — an Imperial bounty of 3,000 g raises Deep-Kin regard by +12, which puts a Dunmer at disposition 6 at 18 against a hostile_below_disposition of 15, so a war-brood camp that was hostile is not, with the archetype, moveset and statblock ids unchanged. The schema has no ar3 field, so it is recorded here and in RI-CRM01 M12. The crossing is verified as a threshold computation; the encounter it should flip does not exist to be observed.

notes: ONE THING WORTH SAYING PLAINLY, because a FAIL at 2/10 will read as a verdict on effort and it is not. This is the most instrumented piece I have measured: 42 outputs, three probe suites, 191 self-assertions, and three genuine defects found in the reference items themselves — one of which (RI-STL01 2's light exponent) I recomputed independently and which is real. The lock ruling is exemplary work: a deterministic skill gate, a real timed interaction with a measured 44 ms window at the requirement and 378 ms at mastery, 719 hand-authored ward angles that reject uniformity at chi-square 226.1, and an RNG counter that does not move once across the whole interaction. Seam S21 was applied rather than copied: the die was deleted where failure is a retry and kept where being caught is permanent, and I measured the surviving die working across 300 attempts. The property data is the best in the repository. What failed is not care and it is not craft. It is that the piece built its systems as modules with harness entry points and never took the last step of making any entity in the running game read them, and then measured the modules and reported the result as the game. The distance between those two things is the whole verdict, and it is why the corpus now has RI-MTH07.  SCHEMA NOTE: RI-STL01's front matter declares `side: split`, which CORPUS-CONTRACT §2 added to the item enum wave 0; corpus/00-doctrine/verdict.schema.json's reference_items.side enum was never updated to match, so this verdict records RI-STL01 as `neutral` to validate. That mismatch is a corpus defect in the schema, not in the item, and is worth one line of repair.
